topic: Optimal Wordle Strategy: Entropy and Algorithmic Search
target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science majors)

sections.title: Introduction: The Game as a Decision Tree
sections.content: Define Wordle as a search problem within a finite set (approx. 2,300 solutions). Introduce the concept of 'information gain'—how a guess reduces the remaining possibilities.
sections.example: Visualizing a branching tree: Start with 2,300 nodes, each guess acts as a filter that prunes the tree branches.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Entropy
sections.content: Explain Shannon Entropy. In Wordle, high entropy means a word splits the remaining vocabulary into the most equal-sized groups, providing the most information on average.
sections.example: Graphical chart: Comparing 'ARISE' (high entropy, splits set into 100-200 groups) vs 'XYLYL' (low entropy, only checks rare letters).

sections.title: Algorithmic Analysis: Greedy vs. Global Optimal
sections.content: Discuss the 'Greedy' approach (choosing the best word for the current turn) versus looking ahead. Explain why the highest entropy word isn't always the winner, but provides the best path.
sections.example: A robot character 'Bot-Bot' testing the word 'CRANE'. Shows a heat map of letter frequency (E, A, R) vs. position frequency.

sections.title: Putting it Together: Strategy Implementation
sections.content: Synthesize the strategy: Use high-frequency letter distributions (E, A, R, I, O, T, N, S) in the first move to maximize entropy, then shift to candidate elimination.
sections.example: Step-by-step animation: Guess 1 (CRANE) -> Feedback (C-gray, R-green, A-yellow...) -> Filter list -> Pick Guess 2 based on highest remaining entropy.

sections.title: Conclusion and Practical Takeaways
sections.content: Summarize the 'Optimal Wordle' heuristic: 1. Maximize unique letter coverage; 2. Prioritize common vowels/consonants; 3. Use the feedback to mathematically isolate the solution.
sections.example: A quick recap screen: An 'Optimal Strategy Cheat Sheet' featuring an owl icon (the symbol of wisdom) showing the top 3 starting words.
